subject: Maths
title: Completing the square
subtitle: Quadratic Equations · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can write a quadratic expression in completed square form.

key_vocab.definition: Completing the square rewrites ax² + bx + c in the form (x + p)² + q. This reveals the vertex (turning point) of the parabola.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can write a quadratic expression in completed square form.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Completing the square -- Completing the square rewrites ax² + bx + c in the form (x + p)² + q. This reveals the vertex (turning point) of the parabola.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
x² + bx + c = (x + &frac{b}{2})² + c − (&frac{b}{2})²
x² + bx + c = (x + &frac{b}{2})² + c − &frac{b²}{4}
Halve b for the bracket; subtract the square for q

Key examples:
  ✓ x² + 6x + 5 = (x + 3)² − 4  (half of 6 is 3, 5 − 9 = −4)
  ✓ x² − 4x + 1 = (x − 2)² − 3  (half of −4 is −2, 1 − 4 = −3)
  ✓ x² + 8x = (x + 4)² − 16  (no constant: q = −16)
  ✗ x² + 6x + 5 = (x + 6)² + 5  (must halve the coefficient)
  ✗ x² + 6x + 5 = (x + 3)² + 5  (forgot to subtract 9)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – positive coefficient of x
  Write x² + 8x + 10 in completed square form.
  Half of 8 is 4, so bracket is (x + 4)²
  (x + 4)² = x² + 8x + 16, so subtract 16
  x² + 8x + 10 = (x + 4)² + 10 − 16 = (x + 4)² − 6
  (x + 4)² − 6
  (The vertex is at (−4, −6).)

Example 2 – negative coefficient of x
  Write x² − 6x + 2 in completed square form.
  Half of −6 is −3, so bracket is (x − 3)²
  (x − 3)² = x² − 6x + 9, so subtract 9
  x² − 6x + 2 = (x − 3)² + 2 − 9 = (x − 3)² − 7
  (x − 3)² − 7
  (The minimum value of this expression is −7.)

sections.title: Positive x coefficient
sections.content:
Write in completed square form (x + p)² + q.

(a) x² + 4x + 1
(b) x² + 6x + 7
(c) x² + 10x + 20
(d) x² + 2x − 3

sections.title: Negative x coefficient
sections.content:
Write in completed square form.

(a) x² − 4x + 3
(b) x² − 8x + 10
(c) x² − 2x − 5
(d) x² − 12x + 30

sections.title: No constant term
sections.content:
Complete the square.

(a) x² + 6x
(b) x² − 10x
(c) x² + 14x
(d) x² − 20x

sections.title: Solving equations
sections.content:
Solve by completing the square.

(a) x² + 6x + 5 = 0
(b) x² − 4x − 12 = 0
(c) x² + 2x − 8 = 0
(d) x² − 10x + 9 = 0

sections.title: Finding the vertex
sections.content:
Complete the square and state the minimum point (vertex).

(a) x² + 4x + 7
(b) x² − 6x + 11
(c) x² + 8x + 20
(d) x² − 2x − 3
(e) x² + 12x + 32

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ To complete the square, halve the coefficient of x
✗ x² + 6x + 5 = (x + 6)² + 5
✓ (x + 3)² = x² + 6x + 9
✗ x² + 6x + 5 = (x + 3)² + 5
✓ The vertex of (x + p)² + q is at (−p, q)

teacher_sections.title: Teacher Key & Mark Scheme
teacher_sections.content:
Award marks for correct working and final answers.

Positive x coefficient:
  (a) (x + 2)² − 3
  (b) (x + 3)² − 2
  (c) (x + 5)² − 5
  (d) (x + 1)² − 4

Negative x coefficient:
  (a) (x − 2)² − 1
  (b) (x − 4)² − 6
  (c) (x − 1)² − 6
  (d) (x − 6)² − 6

No constant term:
  (a) (x + 3)² − 9
  (b) (x − 5)² − 25
  (c) (x + 7)² − 49
  (d) (x − 10)² − 100

Solving equations:
  (a) x = −1 or x = −5
  (b) x = 6 or x = −2
  (c) x = 2 or x = −4
  (d) x = 9 or x = 1

Finding the vertex:
  (a) (x+2)² + 3; vertex (−2, 3)
  (b) (x−3)² + 2; vertex (3, 2)
  (c) (x+4)² + 4; vertex (−4, 4)
  (d) (x−1)² − 4; vertex (1, −4)
  (e) (x+6)² − 4; vertex (−6, −4)
